title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
statement: You get an unsorted list of integers. Find the length of the longest run of values that follow each other with no gaps, such as 5, 6, 7, 8. The run does not need to be in order in the list. Aim for linear time, so sorting is not the goal.

example.caption: The values 1, 2, 3, 4 are all present, even though they sit apart in the list. The run is 4 long.

idea.sentence: Put every number in a set. Only start counting at a number whose predecessor is missing, then walk upward. Every number is walked over at most once.

jargon.plain: A number x where x minus 1 is not in the set. Every run has exactly one.
Counted over the whole input instead of one step. A single walk can be long, but all walks together touch each number once.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of numbers, e.g. [100,4,200,1,3,2]

vars.meaning: number of integers in the list

compare.bruteLabel: Count a run from every number

rows.name: Count from every number
rows.note: On 1, 2, ..., n the walk from 1 is n long, from 2 is n−1 long, and so on. That adds up to about n²/2 lookups.

rows.name: Sort, then scan
rows.note: Sorted neighbours reveal runs. The sort dominates.

rows.name: Set, run starts only
rows.note: Each number is skipped in one lookup, or walked over once inside a single run. About 2n lookups in all.

fast.takeaway: The trap is counting from every number. Skipping the numbers that have a predecessor makes every run get walked once.

stages.title: Build the set
stages.note: Every number goes in a set. Lookups are one step and duplicates vanish.

stages.title: Is it a run start?
stages.note: If x − 1 is in the set, x is inside a run. Skip it. Otherwise x begins a run.

stages.title: Walk up
stages.note: From the start, move to x+1, x+2, ... while each is in the set. The distance walked is the run length.

stages.title: Keep the best
stages.note: Compare this run length with the longest so far.

edges.title: Empty list
edges.why: No numbers means no run. The best stays at zero.

edges.title: All duplicates
edges.why: A duplicate is not the next number. The set keeps one 1, so the run is one long.

edges.title: Negatives
edges.why: Predecessor and successor work the same below zero. The run is −3, −2, −1.

edges.title: Far apart values
edges.why: The size of the numbers never matters. Only whether a neighbour is present.

gotchas.text: The O(n²) trap: starting a walk from every number. A run of length n then gets walked n times, from every position inside it. The x − 1 check is what prevents it.
Loop over the set, not over nums. With many repeats of one run start, looping over nums would walk that run again for each copy.
Range over the map gives random order. The answer does not depend on order, so it does not matter, but a trace can differ between runs.
The built-in max needs Go 1.21 or newer. On older versions write the comparison by hand.

recap.key: A number starts a run only when its predecessor is absent. Walk up from run starts, so each number is touched about once.
moves: Put all numbers in a set
For each x, skip it if x − 1 is in the set
Otherwise walk up while x+1, x+2, ... exist
